title: Level 4 (Expert) - D-2
notes:
West leads the ♣J against 6♠. If South instinctively covers West's ♣J with dummy's ♣K or ♣Q, East will win the ♣A leaving the contract with no chance against best defense. Even if a defender has club length and the ♦KQ, a diamond shift will break up any squeeze (East could otherwise be trump squeezed).

South's only real chance is to play a low club from dummy at trick 1. West would not lead the ♣J if he held the ♣A, especially against a slam, so South must hope that East's ♣A is either singleton or doubleton. If West continues clubs, South should follow through with his plan and duck again in the dummy. In the actual layout South is rewarded as East must play the ♣A as South ruffs. Dummy's ♣K and ♣Q can later be used to discard South's 2 diamond losers.

If West plays any other suit at trick 2, South can win and ruff a club himself in the hope of bringing down the doubleton ♣A. South can draw trump and pitch his diamond losers on dummy's clubs as before.
